description:
The surah that proclaims God to be the Lord of the heavenly ascents, **Lofty Stations**, the points of rising from which the angels ascend to God. It takes is named after the phrase "of lofty stations" (dhi al-ma'ārij) in verse 3. The surah describes the Day of Judgement (verse 8 ff.). One of the opponents of the Prophet challenged him to hasten the punishment they had been threatened with (verse 1), so the foolishness of the disbelievers in denying the Resurrection (verse 6) is exposed (verse 36 ff.). The people who will be granted the Garden are described (verse 22 ff.).
The surah is also known as Elevations, Staircases Upward, The Ascending Steps, The Heavenly Ascents, The Ladders, The Stairways, The Steps, The Ways of Ascent

2.1: Or 'bound to befall the faithless—which none can avert—from Allah…'

39.1: That is, from a drop of sperm.

translations.1: An asker asked for a punishment bound to befall
translations.2: —which none can avert from the faithless—<{["F", 1]}>
translations.3: from Allah, Lord of the lofty stations.
translations.4:
The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him
  in a day whose span is
   fifty thousand years.
translations.5: So _be patient_, with a patience that is graceful.
translations.6: Indeed they see it to be far off,
translations.7: and We see it to be near.
translations.8: The day when the sky will be like molten copper,
translations.9: and the mountains like [tufts of] dyed wool,
translations.10:
and no friend will inquire
  about [the welfare of his] friend,
translations.11:
[though] they will be placed within each other's sight.
 The guilty one will wish he could ransom himself
   from the punishment of that day
  at the price of his children,
translations.13: his kin which had sheltered him
translations.14:
and all those who are upon the earth,
  if that might deliver him.
translations.15: Never! Indeed it is a blazing fire,
translations.17:
It invites him who has turned back [from the truth]
   and forsaken [it],
translations.19: Indeed man has been created covetous:
translations.20: anxious when an ill befalls him
translations.21: and grudging when good comes his way
translations.23: those who are persevering in their prayers
translations.24: and in whose wealth there is a known right
translations.25: for the beggar and the deprived,
translations.26: and who affirm the Day of Retribution,
translations.27:
and those who are
    apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord
translations.28:
(there is indeed
   no security from the punishment of their Lord)
translations.29: and those who guard their private parts
translations.30:
(except from their spouses and their slave women,
   for then they are not blameworthy;
translations.31:
but whoever seeks beyond that
   —it is they who are the transgressors)
translations.32: and those who keep their trusts and covenants,
translations.33: and those who are observant of their testimonies,
translations.34: and those who are watchful of their prayers.
translations.35: They will be in gardens, held in honour.
translations.36:
What is the matter with the faithless
    that they scramble toward _you_
translations.37: from the left and the right in batches?
translations.38:
Does each man among them hope
   to enter the garden of bliss?
translations.39: Never! Indeed We created them from what they know.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.40:
So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests
  that We are able
translations.41:
to replace them by [others] better than them
   and We are not to be outmaneuvered.
translations.42:
So leave them to gossip and play
  until they encounter their day,
   which they are promised:
translations.43:
the day when they emerge from the graves,
    hastening,
   as if racing toward a target,
translations.44:
with a humbled look [in their eyes],
   overcast by abasement.
 That is the day they had been promised.
